prompt: Walk a ResultSet-style cursor with the while(next()) idiom. Complete collectNames and count in ResultCursor, then run the tests.
explanation: A JDBC ResultSet is a cursor parked just before the first row, which is why every read loop is written as while (rs.next()) rather than a counting for loop: next() both advances and reports whether a row is there. Reading a column before the first next() throws, so the read always belongs inside the loop body. A cursor is forward-only and single-use -- once next() returns false the rows are gone, which is why each test builds a fresh one.
hints: The loop shape is while (c.next()) { ... } -- next() moves onto a row and tells you whether one exists.
Read columns only inside the loop body, after next() has returned true.
count needs no column reads at all: just increment a counter each time round the loop.
